stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for agent-assisted purchases
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, letting agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and Dots complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections. It is starting with a limited rollout to US Pro subscribers.
stories.more: ChatGPT Wallet gives agents inside ChatGPT Work, Codex, and Dots a way to complete purchases on a user's behalf. Each purchase requires user approval and relies on existing card protections rather than a new payment system. The feature is starting with a limited rollout to US Pro subscribers rather than a full launch. It is part of a broader push by OpenAI to let its agents act as shopping assistants that can check out directly for users.

stories.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs into factory software
stories.summary: Anthropic launched Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin connecting the AI to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, and Infor with 17 skills for drafting quotes and managing suppliers after human approval.
stories.more: Claude for Manufacturing connects directly to factory software including Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, and Infor. It includes 17 specialized skills that let the AI draft quotes, compare suppliers, and place backup orders when deliveries are delayed, with every action requiring human approval. The plugin does not yet control physical machines on the factory floor. Anthropic is separately developing a Model Hardware Standard intended for that kind of physical control in the future.

stories.title: Startup uses AI microdramas to bring more Black stories to Hollywood
stories.summary: The startup Mansa is using AI-generated microdramas as proofs of concept for Black-audience stories it says are disappearing from Hollywood, though critics call the approach exploitative.
stories.more: The startup Mansa is producing AI-generated microdramas that it says demonstrate demand for stories centered on Black audiences, at a time when Wired reports such roles are disappearing from Hollywood. Mansa frames the microdramas as proofs of concept it can pitch to studios or investors. Critics quoted in the piece argue the approach amounts to the studio selling out rather than genuinely expanding opportunities for Black creators and actors. Further detail on Mansa's size, funding, or specific projects was not included in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Commentary mounts over Jensen Huang's resignation and Nvidia scandal
stories.summary: Outlets continued dissecting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and the personal scandals surrounding it, with commentary on his China dealings and legacy, though no major new facts emerged.
stories.more: Huang resigned from Nvidia's top position on Thursday, and commentators say a bigger story may still unfold around the company's dealings in China and the US government's scrutiny of them. Separate commentary focused on the personal scandals that accompanied his exit, including reports of multiple affairs. A Wired essay argued that Huang, known for his storytelling as a founder, has not been able to spin his way out of the scandals. None of the coverage introduced confirmed new facts beyond the resignation itself and the scrutiny already underway.

stories.title: Meta's Muse agent can now call businesses for you
stories.summary: Meta's AI agent Muse can now call businesses like cable providers and restaurants for its over 10 million users, though some companies hang up once they detect an AI.
stories.more: Meta's Muse agent can now place phone calls to businesses, such as cable providers or restaurants, on behalf of paying US subscribers. Meta's AI chief Alexandr Wang says Muse already has more than 10 million users. The feature puts Muse alongside Google Gemini, Instinct, and xAI's Grok Bot, which offer similar business-calling capabilities. Many businesses reportedly hang up as soon as they detect they are talking to an AI.

stories.title: US agencies' generative AI use nears 70% as unions push guardrails
stories.summary: Nearly 70% of US government agencies now use generative AI, even as public-sector unions increasingly win protections against AI surveillance and automated firings.
stories.more: US public-sector unions are increasingly winning protections against AI-driven surveillance and automated firings, according to The Decoder. In Oakland, a strike vote forced the city to adopt retraining programs instead of layoffs. A transport union in Ohio won veto power over the introduction of autonomous vehicles, and California passed a ban on so-called bossware. These guardrails are emerging even as nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI.

stories.title: Ex-OpenAI researcher says he found Blackwell traces in Chinese AI models
stories.summary: Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue says forensic analysis of model weights shows DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group used Nvidia Blackwell GPUs despite US export controls.
stories.more: Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher, says he has produced the first technical evidence that Chinese AI labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group used Nvidia's latest Blackwell GPUs despite US export controls. His method reads characteristic chip signatures directly from the published weights of the models rather than relying on self-reported hardware claims. He estimates that the hardware behind the five training runs he examined cost more than half a billion dollars.
